attacksRun.attack: Does the version integer moving to 3 create a bare-token collision the subject failed to sweep - the exact failure mode CLAUDE-ALHG-V2-M-1 recorded, one generation on?
attacksRun.result: REFUTED. This was the primary attack and the most likely place for the candidate to break, because v2's defect was precisely a sweep that was not re-run when the integer moved. At integer 3 the newly dangerous lineage is anti-lockstep-leftover-join.v3. The subject qualifies that name fully in all 21 occurrences, carries the guard on basedOn.leftoverJoinV3.role, and adds a matching authorityClaim disclaimer that did not exist in v2. attacksRun.attack: Is the seven-classes claim in remainderAfterThisCorpus true against the contract's own bytes, or does it under-count so that some class is silently treated as exhausted? failsIf[18] makes this a self-declared failure condition.
attacksRun.result: REFUTED, and this is the finding I most expected to make. A keyword pass for every/all/each/any flags eleven of eleven classes, which would suggest the split is wrong. Reading the intents refutes the keyword pass. The four unmarked classes use their quantifier distributively over a list the intent has already closed: CC-3 enumerates 'seq repeats, gaps, decreases; frames replayed after their state window; frames after shutdownAck' and then says 'Each is RF-7 typed'; CC-8 enumerates four smuggling attempts then 'Each is RF-5'; CC-10 enumerates five mismatch shapes then 'Each is RF-3'. CC-11's 'any' quantifies over receivers, not over fixture cases, and the intent explicitly bounds its own case set to 'the exercised vectors and nothing more'. The seven marked classes by contrast carry quantifiers that generate unenumerated members - CC-1 'every reachable total ordering' over an undefined reachable set, CC-2 'every byte offset', CC-4 'EVERY channel state', CC-5 'far over the operative bound' where the bound is not numerically defined, CC-6 'second hello in every state', CC-7 open-ended homoglyph and normalisation categories, CC-9 'every run' plus 'pathological flush patterns'. The seven/four split is correct and is the discriminating reading, not the convenient one.

decision.rationale: Both predecessor findings are landed in the remedied form, and landed by the stronger of the two options the M-1 remedy offered. The attack most likely to succeed - that the version integer moving from 2 to 3 would re-create the very collision v2 was rejected for - fails against the bytes: the sweep was re-executed, the newly colliding v3 lineage is fully qualified in all twenty-one occurrences and guarded, and the two newly non-colliding guards were pruned. The seven-class quantifier split, which a keyword scan would wrongly condemn, is correct on a careful reading of the contract's own intents. Every digest recomputes, every commit resolves, every golden is byte-exact, every quotation is verbatim, and the candidate claims no authority it has not earned. Five advisories travel as honesty work; none rises to SHOULD-FIX.
